components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #1F4FD1; color: #fff; min-height: 48px; padding: 10px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; font: 600 17px Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #173C9E; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.description: Ink code viewer line with gutter and syntax hues.
components.css: .ds-code { background: #0E1117; color: #E6EAF2; font: 13px/20px monospace; padding: 8px 0; display: flex; } .ds-gutter { width: 28px; text-align: right; padding-right: 8px; margin-right: 8px; color: #8A93A6; border-right: 1px solid rgba(230,234,242,0.12); } .ds-kw { color: #8FAAFF; } .ds-str { color: #F2C94C; }

narrative.overview: Review is proofreading. A machine sets a first proof, the user marks corrections in pencil, and the marks are typeset into code. The interface is the galley: a cool proof-white ground (or its ink-dark twin), near-black ink for text, and two pencils. Blue pencil means "you can tap this." Red pencil means "correct or delete." Nothing else carries those meanings.
keyCharacteristics: Two schemes (proof-white, ink) resolved once at launch from Appearance; role names identical in both.
Blue = action, red = correct/delete, each exclusive to that meaning.
Five detected element classes are five pencil marks, each with a 3-letter abbreviation so class is never color alone.
Mono slug line voice for status, counts, labels, and code; Roboto for everything spoken.
Flat by default; a hairline is the primary divider.

rules.name: The Two Pencils Rule
rules.body: Blue is only for what can be tapped; red is only for correcting or removing. Never use either for decoration or for a class mark.

rules.name: The Mark Never Alone Rule
rules.body: A class is always color plus abbreviation (and its word in the tray). Selected chips are filled, not only recolored.

rules.name: The Always-Ink Code Rule
rules.body: Code is read on the fixed ink palette, whatever the OS scheme.

rules.name: The Slug Line Rule
rules.body: Machine-ish facts (counts, status, labels) are set in the mono slug; human sentences in Roboto.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a hairline or a tonal step before reaching for the raised shadow.

dos: Do draw colors from the resolved colors, marks, and code exports; never hardcode hex in screens.
Do keep 48dp minimum for anything tappable.
Do pair every class color with its abbreviation.
Do keep the code screen on the ink palette.
donts: Don't use blue for anything that is not an action, or red for anything that is not correct/delete.
Don't use the pastel-green pill utility look; no pill shapes.
Don't convey state by color alone; selection is also filled or ruled.
Don't add elevation to regions that a hairline can separate.
